# Jubilees Chapter 44 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 44:4 — "multitude of nations"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "his seed shall become a multitude of nations" | Literal; follows the Hebrew melo' ha-goyim |
| LOGOS | "his descendants will become a multitude of nations" | Modern formal |
| PNEUMA | "His descendants will fill the nations" | Compressed; loses "multitude" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "a multitude of nations." The Ge'ez parallels the Hebrew melo' ha-goyim precisely. PNEUMA's "fill the nations" misses the "multitude" dimension.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 44:9 — "hamstrung oxen" vs. "lame oxen"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "in their wantonness they lame oxen" | Present tense; follows traditional KJV |
| LOGOS | "in their wantonness they hamstrung oxen" | Past tense; "hamstrung" is more precise |
| PNEUMA | "they mutilated animals out of spite" | Generalizes |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "hamstrung oxen." "Hamstrung" is the specific action (severing the tendon), which is what the Ge'ez describes. EMET's "lame" is vaguer; PNEUMA's "mutilated" is an overstatement.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 44:10 — Judah blessing — register

All three translators agreed on the Judah blessing text substantially. PNEUMA's "grip the throats of your enemies" was considered but the formal "your hand shall be on the neck of your enemies" was preferred.

**Status:** Resolved: formal register adopted.
